standard-dialogue.npc: Ah, greetings. What can I do for you?

steps.npc: I'm Madam Sikaro.
Why shouldn't it be? You asked who I was, and I answered.

steps.player: I was hoping to learn something about you, like what you were doing here...!

steps.npc: Well, perhaps next time you'll ask a more direct question.
Making a wizard hideout.
A wizard hideout! You know how some wizards have their own towers? Think that but underground.

steps.player: So why not just get a tower?

steps.npc: Land price. Kingdoms want you to pay an extortionate amount of money to build on 'their' land, it turns out.

steps.player: So instead you ended up in the basement of a tavern.

steps.npc: Yep. Camarst said I could have it as long as I don't hurt any of his customers too badly.
Not that I actually plan to hurt any of his customers.

options.text: I have this part that looks like it's from a weapon...
options.condition: If the player has a part of the Voidwaker:

steps.text: If the player has less than three parts of the Voidwaker:

steps.player: I have this part that looks like it's from a weapon...

steps.npc: Ah yes, that does look like a part of a particularly powerful weapon.

steps.player: Can I do anything with it?

steps.npc: You? Perhaps not, though if you could bring me all three pieces, I suspect I could put it back together for you.
There should be a hilt, a blade and a conduit gemstone. Oh, and I'll want 500,000 coins as payment as well. Good hunting!

steps.player: Do you know where I could find the other parts?

steps.npc: I suspect the Wilderness would be a good place to start. There are monsters out there that have grown immense over time.
Seeking out the strongest of them is where I'd start, anyway.

steps.text: If the player has all three parts of the Voidwaker:

steps.player: I have these parts of a weapon, do you think you could assemble it for me?

steps.npc: Hmm... yes, these are the parts of a particularly powerful weapon indeed. I can reassemble it... for a fee, of course. 500,000 coins, no less.

steps.text: If the player has less than 500,000 coins:

steps.player: I don't have that much on me...

steps.npc: Well, if you come across some more, come find me again.

steps.text: If the player has at least 500,000 coins:

steps.prompt: Have Madam Sikaro assemble the Voidwaker for 500,000 coins?

steps.text: Madam Sikaro takes the components off you and, in a flash of white light, fuses them together to form the Voidwaker.

steps.npc: Curious, you come to me with all of the parts and the coin, yet you change your mind at the last second.
I do rather get the feeling you're toying with me. Very well, I shall do my part in playing with you.

steps.text: You feel the contents of your inventory shift slightly.

steps.npc: Now, do talk to me again if you'd like to proceed more sensibly.

options.text: What are you doing with the money?
options.condition: If the player has had Madam Sikaro assemble the Voidwaker:

steps.player: What are you doing with the money from combining the Voidwaker?

steps.npc: I'll spend some of it improving the hideout. The rest on general expenses.
Living isn't free, you know? A woman my age has expenses. Food, clothing, protection... It all adds up.
You walked up to me just to say goodbye? Ok, sure, goodbye.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: So what exactly is this sword, anyway?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Well, that largely depends on who you ask and when you ask it. The sword is not unique, but many like it have been referenced in folktales.
Some tell of great and prideful warriors roaming the lands, cutting down all who oppose them in great crashes of lightning.
Others tell of lovers, one bound by oath, the other free as the wind, cruely torn apart by fate.
Others still tell of three great beasts that alone were powerful, but combined could destroy Gielinor.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: Are we still talking about the sword?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Amazingly, yes. In all of these tales, the sword is there, potential shining through the metal, thunder rolling in its wake.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: Are any of these tales... true?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Oh, I'm sure there are elements of the truth buried in there, but folklore being what it is, I'm inclined to not believe any of it.
Aside from the bit where it can summon lightning. It can absolutely do that.

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.player: What about the name? You called it Voidwaker?

standard-dialogue-using-the-voidwaker-on.npc: Well, in a lot of these tales, it's only ever reffered to as someone's sword. Like, [player name]'s sword.
So, I chose a name for it.
There are multiple reasons. I suppose you could say the sword is so powerful that it leaves a void in its wake.

standard-dialogue-using-any-other-item-o.npc: No thank you, I'm currently on a diet.
